insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (Base Sum Insured + NCB; plus Refill benefit as applicable)

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: 3.6. Refill We will add an amount equal to the base sum insured, after the first claim is paid... b. Benefit applies for any illness (same or different).
great.explanation: After the first claim is paid, an extra amount equal to the Base Sum Insured is added in the same policy year. It can be used for any illness including the same illness, which is stronger than many restore benefits that restrict to unrelated illnesses.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: 4.1.1. Pre-existing Diseases (Code–Excl01): a. Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Expenses for pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage. This is within the common 2–4 year range in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: 4.1.2. Specified disease/procedure waiting period (Code- Excl02) a. Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a standard waiting period for such conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 4.1.3. 30-day waiting period (Code- Excl03): a. Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days... shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days, but accidents are covered from day one. This is the usual market-standard initial waiting period.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: 3.3. ... 60 days before date of admission and 180 days after date of discharge IF these are related to the condition for which hospital admission claim is paid.
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before admission are covered if related to the hospitalization. This helps pay for diagnostics and consultations leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: 3.3. ... 60 days before date of admission and 180 days after date of discharge IF these are related to the condition for which hospital admission claim is paid.
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 180 days after discharge are covered if related to the hospitalization. This reduces out-of-pocket costs for follow-up treatment and medicines.

good.name: No Claim Bonus
good.quote: 3.5. No Claim Bonus (NCB) For every claim free year, we will add 20% of expiring policy base sum insured as NCB, maximum up to 100%.
good.explanation: For each claim-free year, the Base Sum Insured increases by 20%, up to a maximum of 100%. This can meaningfully increase your available cover over time if you don’t claim.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: 3.9. Home Care / Domiciliary Treatment... We will pay for Pre & Post hospitalization benefit as per section 3.3 for Home Care / Domiciliary Treatment.
good.explanation: Home care/domiciliary treatment is covered, along with pre- and post-hospitalization benefits as per Section 3.3. This is useful when treatment is medically required at home instead of a hospital.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: For Variant 2023 there is a room type capping up to Shared Room. 20% co-payment will apply in case of higher room category
bad.explanation: Room eligibility is capped up to a Shared Room for Variant 2023. Choosing a higher room category triggers extra costs (including a 20% co-payment), which can make hospitalizations significantly more expensive.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: If you opt for a Hospital room which is higher than the eligible room category as specified in your Policy Schedule, then We will pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses... (Eligible Room Rent limit / Room Rent actually incurred) * total Associated Medical Expenses
bad.explanation: If you take a room higher than your eligible category, the insurer pays associated medical expenses only on a pro-rated basis using the stated formula. This can sharply reduce claim payouts beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Annexure I - List I – Expenses not covered... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 68 VASOFIX SAFETY
bad.reference: Annexure I (List I – Expenses not covered)
bad.explanation: Consumables like gloves, masks and vasofix are listed as not covered. These items are commonly billed during hospitalization and can add to out-of-pocket expenses.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: For Variant 2023... 20% co-payment will apply in case of higher room category
bad.explanation: A 20% co-payment applies if a higher room category than the eligible one is used (Variant 2023). This means you must bear 20% of admissible expenses in that situation, increasing your share of the bill.
